Eve — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up top, details and examples below. Attaching our retention matrix for reference.

TL;DR (default behavior for Hosted API):
- Full request payloads (user inputs + system prompts): retained by default for 30 days
- Final model outputs (completed responses): retained by default for 30 days
- Streaming partial tokens: not persisted in long-term storage by default; streamed buffer is transient and discarded after the connection completes unless customer enables recording
- Tool/function call payloads: treated like outputs and retained by default for 30 days
- KV cache / runtime-only caches: ephemeral (kept in memory/GPU); not written to durable logs unless explicit debug capture is enabled

Examples:
1) Simple chat (no streaming): user sends prompt -> we store the request and the final generated answer in the request/response store. Both are retained 30d and encrypted at rest.
2) Chat with streaming enabled: as tokens stream to the client, we do not write those incremental tokens to durable logs by default. After the session finishes we store the final joined response (the same artifact a non-streaming call would have) and that final output is retained 30d. If the customer enables "session recording" in Console, streaming buffers are persisted and marked in the record (see matrix).
3) Tool call / function: the tool request, the tool response, and any structured outputs (JSON) are considered generated outputs and are retained with the final output set (30d) unless the customer disables retention for their workspace.

Deletion / Erasure:
- Auto-delete: items older than 30 days are automatically purged by the retention job.
- On-demand erasure: customers can request immediate deletion for a workspace via the Console or by filing an erasure ticket with our support portal. We run a deletion workflow that removes entries from the request/response store and queues tombstone tasks for secondary indices; completion is visible in the audit log. Typical turnaround for hosted accounts is 48–72 hours (expedited paths available under contract).
- Auditability: erasure actions are recorded in immutable audit logs with a job id; we can provide proof-of-deletion artifacts for GDPR/DSARs (hashes and deletion job ids) as part of enterprise support.

Residency / encryption:
- Default hosted region for BrightBank pilot will be us-east-1 unless you request eu-west-1.
- Data is encrypted at rest with customer-facing KMS; for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM.

I'll loop Kim on operational pieces (runbook, deletion job ids) and Marissa on policy language for contracts. If you'd like a short call to walk through a concrete flow (with a sample streamed session) I'm available tomorrow afternoon.

Regards,

Eve — adding some operational clarifications and a short checklist so your security team can map answers to their questionnaire.

Operational clarifications:
- What "retained by default" means: for hosted customers, the Platform writes request/response records into our telemetry store and marks them with a retention TTL. Those records are logically deleted when the TTL expires and then physically erased by the background purge within 7 days of logical deletion.
- Streaming internals: streaming uses an in-memory buffer on an inference node; we do not replicate that buffer to durable object storage by default. If a customer enables debug recording we capture the buffer as a separate "session artifact" (flagged in the artifact metadata).
- Cache behavior: runtime caches (KV entries used for acceleration) are not treated as logs; they are evicted according to cache policy. If a customer requests cache persistence for their Dedicated cluster (for warm-start), those persisted items are treated as customer-managed artifacts and have separate retention controls.

Checklist items for BrightBank security doc: 
- Default retention window (hosted): 30 days (auto-purge thereafter).
- Audit evidence available: deletion job id, tombstone timestamps, S3 object-hash proofs for deleted objects (available for enterprise support packs).
- Region options: us-east-1 (default), eu-west-1 (on request).
- Erasure SLA (hosted): standard 72 hours; expedited 24 hours with enterprise contract.

If you confirm BrightBank wants eu-west-1 residency and enterprise-level proof-of-deletion artifacts, we will prepare contract language and an SOW for the expedited erasure SLA.

Thanks,
